title: Onboard hypatia-lite-7b v1.0 — perf metadata & changelog automation
author: Asha Raman
description: This PR adds hypatia-lite-7b v1.0 to the model registry with validated performance profiles, model metadata, and automation to include the model in the changelog/release notes pipeline. Motivation: hypatia-lite-7b is a new 7B family optimized for low-latency inference; onboarding lets customers select the model from the Redwood model catalog and leverages automated perf profiles to route to the correct serving kernels. What this PR does: - Add model metadata (models/hypatia-lite/metadata.yaml) with schema fields: model name, version, tokenizer, repository, recommended quantization, supported sequence lengths, default batch sizing, and compatibility tags. - Add performance profiles (perf/hypatia-lite-7b-v1.0/profiles.json) produced by the perf-lab harness: p50/p95 latency, throughput for common batch sizes, memory footprint for asm/qat/quant variants. Profiles include target hardware mappings (A100-80GB, H100-80GB, RTX6000). - Wire the model into the changelog automation: update scripts/release/changelog-generator to detect new model folders and auto-generate an entry with standardized metadata pulled from metadata.yaml and perf summary. - Add unit/integration tests: tests/models/test_metadata_schema.py and tests/perf/test_profile_validation.py to ensure metadata and perf JSONs match schema and thresholds. - Update registry index and model-catalog entry (catalog/hypatia-lite-7b-v1.0.json) that drives the docs and API model catalog. Checklist: - [x] metadata.yaml created and schema-validated - [x] perf profiles generated and validated against perf-lab thresholds - [x] changelog-generator augmented and unit-tested - [x] catalog entry added and linked to docs pipeline - [x] CI passing (lint, unit, perf validation) Notes on perf profiles: the perf numbers were produced by perf-lab in benchmark-lab/pr-1124 and include both baseline fp16 and 4-bit quantized profiles. We recommend the quantized profile for cost-sensitive routing and the fp16 profile for latency-sensitive routing. Backwards compatibility and rollout: this PR does not change existing runtime behavior. The changelog automation only appends an entry in the generated release notes; customers will see the new model in the API model catalog after the next release. See linked Linear tasks ENG-1427 for rollout and PM-223 for marketing/release notes copy. CI: the initial workflow had a lint warning (metadata key ordering); fixed in commit 3. Merge: squashed and merged after approvals.
